question.text: Two weights of the mass $m_{1}$ and $m_{2}\left(>m_{1}\right)$ are joined by an inextensible string of negligible mass passing over a fixed frictionless pulley. The magnitude of the acceleration of the loads is

solution.text: According to the question, we can draw the following diagram Here, $T$ is the tension in the string. In equilibrium condition. For mass $m_{1}, \quad T-m_{1} g=m_{1} a$....(i) For mass $m_{2}, \quad m_{2} g-T=m_{2} a$....(ii) After adding Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $$ \begin{aligned} m_{2} g-m_{1} g &=m_{1} a+m_{2} a \\ \left(m_{2}-m_{1}\right) g &=\left(m_{1}+m_{2}\right) a \\ a &=\frac{\left(m_{2}-m_{1}\right)}{\left(m_{1}+m_{2}\right)} g \end{aligned} $$
